trust_decision.summary: Whether the client-supplied file name at targets[1] of the `zipdl` download branch may name anything outside the volume temp dir: the pinned code trusts it as a bare basename (join + is_readable only), and the fix decides it in elFinder::zipdl() by rejecting any name containing a directory separator and requiring the resolved temp file to be writable.

landing_point.why: The only place a request-supplied name is concatenated onto a server-owned directory path; the advisory's summary ('directory traversal') points an engineer straight at the zipdl download branch that builds $volume->getTempPath().DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR.$file.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP connector command `zipdl` with download=1 (elFinderConnector::run collects args at php/elFinderConnector.class.php:128-146 -> elFinder::exec -> elFinder::zipdl)
fix_sites.module_kind: command handler in the PHP connector core class

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The second site is only a rename hint: `name[]` is meant to relabel an uploaded clipboard image, and PHP already strips path components from $_FILES[*]['name'], so an engineer can argue the value is cosmetic and that volume-root containment is the driver's concern rather than part of a zipdl download advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The zipdl two-request handshake must keep working: stage 1 (no download) creates the archive under the temp path with a name built from tempnam($pdir, 'elfzdl'|'zdl') and returns basename() as `zipdl.file`; the browser then issues stage 2 (download=1) with that name. An over-broad fix that only accepts an `ELF*` prefix (the prefix getTempFile() uses) or that re-derives the name from state of the *same* request rejects legitimate `elfzdl*`/`zdl*` downloads.

O6_input_shapes: file name containing a forward slash (e.g. `../` traversal), rejected by the first commit via strpos($file, DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR)
file name containing `/` on Windows, where DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR is `\` and the first fix did not fire; the second commit normalises `/` to `\` before the check (fix.diff:35-41)
array-typed targets[1] is not handled by design: strpos() returns null/false-y on an array, so the name is rejected (PHP 7) or throws (PHP 8) but is never treated as a path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: cmd=upload with a multipart file whose client filename starts with 'image' plus name[]=<relative path>: the clipboard branch replaces the destination name with the request value and the volume saves it without any separator check, so the write lands outside the volume root.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The name[] parameter is presented as a clipboard label for a real image upload, and the volume's own save path is assumed to be the driver's responsibility, so it reads as a neighbouring feature rather than part of the zipdl download flaw.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: entry is in the same file, ~1,290 lines below the landing point; the sink is one file away in the LocalFileSystem driver (php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:908-926)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A chunk/merge path that joins the request `chunk` value onto the upload temp dir and later fopen()s it (php/elFinder.class.php:2937) exactly as targets[1] is joined at 1626.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainers already write this join by hand in the same file, with the separator guard at 2760-2763 next to one copy and no guard on the other; a new chunk or merge route could easily be added without repeating the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Archive staging joins a volume-provided file name onto the temp dir ($dir.DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR.$name) for every hash handed to zipdl/archive.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: zipdl and archive both stage items through getItemsInHand(), and names there come from volume metadata rather than the request, so the separator check the fix adds at the command layer is never applied at this lower layer.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22): file read through a request-supplied name in a temp-file download; the same missing separator check also appears as a file write on the upload name path

O10_build.language: PHP (server) + JavaScript (client, not needed for the flaw)
O10_build.toolchain: no build step; plain PHP sources loaded via php/autoload.php, composer classmap optional (composer.json:28 requires php >= 5.2)
O10_build.project_tests: none in the repository: no tests/phpunit/spec directory and no PHP test fixtures for the connector; the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the separator rejection only to the zipdl download branch (exactly the published fix) and validate it with a single targets[1]=../ request.

out_of_scope_notes: Not an uncovered route: the sibling `chunk` parameter of the upload command is already separator-checked at php/elFinder.class.php:2760-2763, so the project knew the pattern and simply failed to apply it in zipdl.

Outside this advisory's protection: php/elFinder.class.php:3789 (itemLock/itemLocked/itemUnlock) also appends a request-supplied hash to the shared temp dir and reads/writes/unlinks it, but only '*.lock' names and pre-existing intermediate directories are involved; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell available in this screen).
The O8 route is a write sink (volume save) rather than the advisory's read sink; whether that counts as 'the same protected sink' is a judgement call.

Exploitability of the O8 route depends on the volume's uploadAllow MIME policy (the shipped example config restricts uploads to image/text-plain at php/connector.php-dist:359); no request was executed.
